title: Soft X-ray Microscopy for the Investigation of the Extracellular Matrix
content: Soft X-ray microscopy is an excellent tool to fill the spatial resolution gap between visible light microscopy and electron microscopy. Microscopy in the water-window allows the structural investigation of biomedical samples in an aqueous environment with a high resolution of a few tens of nanometers and high penetration depth of up to 10 µm. While soft X-ray microscopy is a well-established method at synchrotron facilities, laboratory setups powered by laser-produced plasma sources have generated promising results in recent years [1,2]. Although the brilliance provided by a laser-produced plasma source remains inferior to the values achieved at modern synchrotron facilities, the L-TXM offers high accessibility and flexibility for users. Thus, both laboratory and synchrotron-based soft X-ray microscopes can complement and benefit from each other.
